Heard Shri Himanshu Raghave, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners, who are 18 in number, Shri Sarvesh Kumar Dubey, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent Nos.3, 4, and 5.
2.

This petition has been filed with the following main prayers:-

sentences.text: Initially, when the writ petition was filed, this Court had directed filing of counter affidavit by National Highway Authority of India (N.H.A.I.) on the pleadings as made in the writ petition.

It was the case of the petitioners as pleaded initially that their respective houses/shops have never been acquired and are proposed to be acquired and demolished for the purpose of alignment/straightening of Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway/National Expressway-6 at Banthra Bazar,
Banthra, Sikanderpur, Sarojini Nagar, Lucknow in order to promote maximum speed of 120 Kilometers per hour in an absolutely arbitrary and irrational manner.

The said decision of demolishing the houses of the petitioners for promoting speed is arbitrary because it may lead to road accidents and may cause fatalities which cannot be the object of a Welfare State.

4. The facts as mentioned in the petition are that the Government of India, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (herein referred to as MORTH) had issued an intention to create an elevated National Expressway (NE-6) and gazette notification was issued for the same.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said Expressway was proposed through 11 villages in Lucknow and 31 villages in Unnao Districts for which 460 Hectares of land was acquired.

Some of the villages being Banthra, Bani, Daatauli,
Kanthha Taura, Neornna, Amarsas and Rawal.
The proposed Expressway would cut down travel time from two hours by NH-25 to 50 minutes in between Kanpur and Lucknow.

The proposed Balram Singh And Others vs Union Of India Thru. Secy. Ministry Road ... on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162603411/
2 Expressway was to have two elevated portions between Amausi and Bani.

entities.text: Balram Singh And Others vs Union Of India Thru. Secy. Ministry Road
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. The petitioners along with their ancestors have been owners and in possession of their respective Abaadi Land over Khasra Nos.449, 463 & 538 in Village Banthra, Sikanderpur since before independence and they have their shops also.
A notification under Section 3A (1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 was issued on 22.02.2023 proposing acquisition of land specified in schedule for building NE-6.
The Objections were invited.
The petitioners preferred objections which were dis-allowed by the Competent Authority.
A report was submitted to the Central Government under Section 3D (1) of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The Central Government thereafter issued the impugned notification on 03.05.2023 under Section 3D(2) of National Highways Act 1956 declaring acquisition and vesting on specified land in the Central government 6.

The petitioners were served with a notice under Section 266 of the Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002 for removing their encroachment on land earmarked for the construction of National Expressway-6.

entities.text: Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners demolished some of their constructions up to the yellow line which was initially marked on their properties.
The petitioners were also issued notice by ADM Land Acquisition Lucknow for producing documents for payment of compensation.
The petitioners, however, are not interested in ex-Gratia payment that was determined for them.
They are entitled to the benefit under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (herein referred as the Act of 2013).

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners being owners of land on which their constructions is situated
have been given compensation only for constructions raised by them on such land.
By the impugned notification, the petitioners' land is being acquired deviating from the original detail project report which did not provide for alignment as shown at the curve at Banthra.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners has repeatedly argued that the National Expressway-6 has been proposed to be constructed only to promote speed of 120 Kilometers per hour which may cause fatalities.

8. The matter has come up before this Court today only because the petitioners have moved an application for urgent hearing and for grant of interim relief alleging therein that the petitioners made a representation on 10.04.2024 along with a copy of the order dated 08.4.2024 to the District Magistrate, Lucknow and also gave a copy of the order to the Project Director, N.H.A.I., Lucknow,
but instead of deciding their representation, the petitioners have come to know that the N.H.A.I./Project Director is proposing to demolish 75 houses at Banthra including the petitioners'
house on Monday i.e. today.
It has been stated in the affidavit filed in support of such application that the news item that was published in the newspapers relating to removal of encroachments/
illegal
constructions
is mis-leading as the petitioners have not raised any illegal constructions and have been in possession of their Abaadi Land since before independence

. 
9. It has also been submitted that by means of a Government Order issued on 30.06.2022, the State of U.P. has proposed to conduct a population survey and documentation of 1,10,313 villages under Section 43(2) of the U.P. Revenue Code 2006.

In respect of the Villages that have been included in Municipal Boards/ Municipality/Nagar Palika etc, the population survey and documentation under Balram Singh And Others vs Union Of India Thru. Secy. Ministry Road ... on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162603411/
3

sentences.text: the 'Swamitva Yojna' has not been carried out of Village-Banthra and letting the respondents to demolish the houses of the petitioners will adversely affect the petitioners rights which would have accrued under the Government Order dated 30.06.2022.

10. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of N.H.A.I. has pointed out that the main relief claimed in the petition is for quashing of the award notified on 03.05.2023 and statutory remedy under Section 3(G)(5) of the N.H.A.I. Act is available.

It has also been stated that the second relief as claimed in the writ petition is also not liable to be granted in so far as the Detailed Project Report for the Expressway having been considered and approved by the Competent Authority is not being deviated in any manner.
11.

Learned counsel for the N.H.A.I. has also placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Union of India Vs. Kushala Shetty and Others (2011) 12 SCC page 69 and paragraph 28 thereof.

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Kushala Shetty and Others (2011) 12 SCC page 69
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. We have gone through the observations laid by the hon'ble Supreme Court in paragraph 28 of the aforesaid judgement quoted herein below:-
"28. Here, it will be apposite to mention that NHAI is a professionally managed statutory body having expertise in the field of development and maintenance of national highways.

The projects involving construction of new highways and widening and development of the existing highways, which are vital for the development of infrastructure in the country, are entrusted to experts in the field of highways.
It comprises of persons having vast knowledge and expertise in the field of highway development and maintenance.
NHAI prepares and implements projects relating to development and maintenance of national highways after thorough study by experts in different fields.
Detailed project reports are prepared keeping in view the relative factors including intensity of heavy vehicular traffic and larger public interest.
The courts are not at all equipped to decide upon the viability and feasibility of the particular project and whether the particular alignment would subserve the larger public interest.
In such matters, the scope of judicial review is very limited.
The court can nullify the acquisition of land and, in the rarest of rare cases, the particular project, if it is found to be ex facie contrary to the mandate of law or tainted due to mala fides.
In the case in hand, neither has any violation of mandate of the 1956 Act been established nor has the charge of malice in fact been proved.

Therefore, the order under challenge cannot be sustained."
13.

In so far as the relief No.3 as claimed in the writ petition is concerned, it can only be granted if relief No.2 is granted and since relief No.2 is not liable to be granted, relief No.3 also cannot be granted.

With regard to the relief No.4 as prayed in the petition regarding restricting speed of motor vehicles in the interest of public safety and convenience, this Court as a policy does not interfere in matters that require expert opinion.

sentences.text: Since the final relief as claimed by the petitioners in the said writ petition cannot be granted interim relief as prayed for in the applications i.e. before us today, should also not be granted.

15. It has also been submitted by learned counsel for N.H.A.I. on the basis of report prepared by the Competent Revenue Officers including area Lekhpal, the concerned representative of the N.H.A.I.
and other Revenue Officers, the petitioners are in occupation of land belonging to the government.
Gata Nos.604, 449, 463 and 538 which are all recorded in the revenue records as government land for which compensation cannot be given to the petitioners either under the Act of 2013 or Act of 2002.

16. It has also been submitted that taking into account the constructions that have been raised by the petitioners, ex-Gratia compensation has been determined for the occupier of such government land by an order dated 09.02.2024, Rs.89,70,471/- has been already deposited before the Competent Authority as per Section 3(H)(1) of N.H.A.I. Act for Village Banthara, Sikanderpur.
Learned counsel for N.H.A.I. has produced before this Court the relevant order determining such compensation dated 09.02.2024 passed by the ADM Land Acquisition, Lucknow, the Competent Authority.
The same is kept on record also the report as submitted by the revenue team along with representative of the N.H.A.I. is also kept on record.
17. This Court is of the considered opinion that since final relief cannot be granted, there is no question of granting interim relief also.

18. This Court after hearing both counsels on merits finds no good ground to interfere in the matter,
hence, the instant writ petition is hereby dismissed.

. 
[Subhash Vidyarthi, J.]

[Sangeeta Chandra,J.] Order Date :- 15.4.2024 -Amit K-
